finding.expected: Enumerate exact bound commit trees recursively, while preserving the existing local-object-only/no-fetch, no-rename-heuristic and deterministic path semantics. Only changed regular blob paths should become ADD/MODIFY/DELETE records; directory tree entries are structural and must not themselves be treated as review material. Add focused regressions with nested repository paths for MODIFY plus ADD/DELETE (including a nested rename normalized as DELETE+ADD) and prove the package/revalidator still satisfy all existing bounds, source-table closure and worktree/config independence. Keep the correction inside TASK-185 scope and do not alter P1A or any lifecycle/provider/Reviewer authority.
finding.issue: The Git material constructor enumerates each commit with "git ls-tree -rz -t --full-tree <commit>" but omits recursive traversal (-r). Therefore a normal changed file below a directory is not materialized. Instead the changed top-level directory appears as a tree entry with a changed tree OID, _view cannot find any child path in the non-recursive mapping, and construction fails as UNSUPPORTED_MATERIAL ("empty changed tree"). The focused tests use only top-level files, so Runtime verification does not exercise the repository-relative nested-path case that TASK-185 must support. This would prevent BP6-P1B from packaging ordinary AIOS changes such as src/aios_renew/*.py and tests/*.py for a repository-blind Reviewer.
